Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/20/2019
Violation Code: 78a81(a)3 - CASING AND CEMENTING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to prevent pollution or diminution of fresh groundwater.
Violation ID: 901194
Permit API: 131-20561
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Meshoppen Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on all (5) wells on the Hunter pad., the Hunter 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H. These SPBUTs are being performed to assess the recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool), deployment performed on all (5) Hunter wells production casing strings. - All (5) wells on the pad are shut in. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a production tank via 2" common vent line. All annuli were closed when I arrived w/ the exception of the 21HC (20x13) annulus and the 6H (9x5) annulus which were opened early.- Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Rep. Brendan Hollerand, Creston Consultant Reps., Shane Reimold and Alex Pashchuk. Starting at approx. 10:00, ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. - The (20x13) annulus vent of the 21HC was opened within first 27 hrs. of SPBUT due to pressures exceeding 30 psi and the 6H (9x5) annulus vent was opened within 13.5 hrs. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/18/2023 to RICE DRILLING B LLC in North Bethlehem Township, Washington county. 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect  brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RICE DRILLING B LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/18/2023
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8153114
Permit API: 125-27720
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: North Bethlehem Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/18/2023
Comments: On 07/18/2023, an incident inspection was conducted at the Ironman Well Site in response to an incident report received by the Department and submitted by EQT on 07/17/2023 (CTS: 373620). I was accompanied by Matt Dracup, PGM (PADEP), Doug Oberdorf, and Jason Nicholson (EQT). Additional EQT and SPSI representatives on site. Stressed vegetation observed on north-northwest facing slope (fill side) of the Ironman pad on 07/14/2023 by an EQT contractor doing a routine site inspection. EQT representative investigated stressed vegetation on 07/17/2023 and identified it as a brine release and notified the Department. It was further investigated by EQT on 07/17/2023 w/ interim remediation activities starting on 07/18/2023. According to EQT, an approx. 5 ft x 2 ft pool of fluid was observed within area of stressed vegetation and fluid was observed sprinkling out. The overall area of stressed vegetation was approximately 25 ft x 25 ft. The release was estimated over a barrel and Act 2 remediation is anticipated. The source of the leak was identified as a small pinhole in cushion elbow at the northern most corner of the pad from the buried common dump line transferring brine flowback from the GPUs to the ASTs; approx. 70 ft northeast, away from the stressed vegetation area. Operator discovery and pre-remediation conductivity levels and incident writeup requested.Inspection observations: Area of stressed vegetation and pooled production fluid observed on fill slope below northwestern edge of pad and below compressor building on the pad. Among pooled fluid, an oily sheen was also observed. The impacted area appeared to be approx. 25 ft. x 25 ft. The area was covered with a plastic tarp upon arriving on site (Photos 1-7). SPSI crew preparing and beginning excavation to locate source of leak and begin remediation measures. Potholes to be dug on pad around approximate area of leak source to gain extent of fluid. Elevated conductivity observed within impacted area yielded readings of 14.62 mS, 9.96 mS. Readings beyond edge of impacted area, on the more northern edge of the area, displayed a reading of 1.87 mS. Additional readings within vegetation beyond edge of affected area were taken and yielded levels of 1.03 and within the area beyond the fence approximately 5 ft. at the bottom of the slope, 1.98 mS was observed within vegetation. Readings taken within the Unnamed Tributary to Daniels Run, below impacted area approximately 125 ft. north of the impacted area. Readings obtained within water and sediment of the stream w/ levels at 0.43-0.86 mS. Readings obtained within retentive berm along southeastern edge of site below pad; readings taken in water and within sediment yielded 0.33 mS and 0.60 mS (8-16). Readings taken at southern corner of the vegetated swales outlet structure, both in and around; readings of 0.46 mS within water and 0.59 mS within mud around the structure observed (17). SPSI began excavating a pothole, approx. 3 ft in depth; pooled fluid observed within. Conductivity reading within excavated hole was 6.30 mS. Vegetated berm adjacent to hole, above impacted area, displayed a reading of 0.34 mS (18-20). Additional readings within vegetation beyond western edge of impacted area displayed 2.21-6.44 mS (21-23). Reading in fluid contained within secondary containment around ASTs w/ level of 7.20 mS. Due to observed release of production fluid within vegetation on site and potential for fluid to impact WOC downslope of impacted area, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued. Additional violations of 78a.66(b)(2) for failure to report within 2 hours, 78a.66(b)1(i), 78a.66(b)1(ii), and 91.33(a) for threatening WOC pollution, 5 gallons not completely contained and failure to report to DEP and downstream users are being issued. Additional follow up inspections to be conducted to monitor WOC downslope of impacted area.

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8272220
Permit API: 015-23981
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wysox Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/27/2026
Comments: On 02/26/2025 Expand representative Steven Moyer reported a discovered release onsite (CTS #395411). He stated "there was a hole in containment. An unknown amount of frack water mixed with stormwater on pad." On 02/27/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection of the Wygrala Well Pad in Wysox Township, Bradford County. The area of the reported release is estimated to be an area of 75x150. Within the 75x150 area the elevated conductivity of the soil varies between 0-4 mS/cm. Approximately 2-3 inches of material had already been excavated and placed into containment onsite. Alderdice, Inc. was onsite removing the material during the inspection. The cause of the release was due to a ripped seam in the pad wide containment. On 04/27/2026 the DEP conducted a follow up inspection. The weather was 52 degrees and sunny. I arrived at 0915 hours. The site appeared stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation onsite. Pooled fluids on the pad surface were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 188-721 us/cm. There was no evidence of any spills or releases. There was one produced fluid tank held within secondary containment. There were several temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment. Recovered material was being removed from the site during the inspection (photo #9). Due to the unknown quantity of the release this has been referred to ECB for Act 2 compliance.Based on the reported release (CTS #395411). The following violations remain open against API #015-23981:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)I departed at 1015 hours.

Comments: On 5/2/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/completions inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 60 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the site, I met Seneca's Company man, Wesley Sammons who described current operations as follows: The Patterson 801 drilling rig is set up on site drilling production on four of five new wells. This rig arrived on site and started drilling on 3/31/2024. The crew was currently drilling the production section on the 75HU well and were in the process of drilling the curve, currently being at 11,444 feet. The lateral section will follow with the total depth expected to be 25,743 feet. After this well, there are two more to follow with this rig drilling just the production sections. The surface and intermediate sections were previously drilled by a different rig. Wes expects it to take until approximately 6/24/2024 for the rig to finish at the site.Wes accompanied me on the site inspection. The rig and ancillary equipment were stationed on secondary containment. Chemicals were staged on secondary containment. There were 10 frac tanks on the northeast side of the rig staged in secondary containment, these being used for various drilling fluids. There were two frac tanks on the southeast side of the rig that were used to store rainwater collected from the pad surface. This water was being used for drilling fluids. The drill cuttings were being solidified with a plant-based substance called slate dry and with wood pellets prior to being transported offsite to a waste disposal facility. I did witness drill cuttings being piled up above the level of the exterior wall of an open-top tank. I discussed keeping the level of the material low enough to allow for necessary free board. During a previous inspection I witnessed elevated conductance water along the north perimeter berm. I did not witness water in this area during this inspection. Following up on a previous inspection, I collected water sample 9551-108 from the sediment basin near the center overflow inlet box and water sample 9551109 from within the outlet pipe at the corresponding drain grate. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Temporary compost filter socks have been installed throughout the construction site. Vegetation is becoming established in recently constructed areas but the requirements for permanent stabilization have not been met yet. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Infiltration berms 2 and 3 and the sedimentation basin do not yet meet the vegetative requirements for permanent stabilization.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3724668 and ID 3736567 for a 6' x 60' puddle of water with elevated conductance and with a white substance in it; discovered on the unprotected pad surface and flowing into the sediment basin during drilling operations. The DEP recommends the following: 1. Prevent water with elevated levels of aluminum from leaving the pad surface, from entering the sediment basin, from leaving the LOD and from infiltrating into the groundwater. 2. Continues the process of determining the source of contamination as witnessed in this and prior inspections. 3. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad and entering the sediment basin. Clean and report as necessary.4. Maintain adequate levels of freeboard in open-topped containers including the half-round dumpsters being used for drill cuttings.5. Continue to monitor the stability and functionality of the sediment traps and sediment basin and repair as necessary.I left the site at 1110 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/18/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 992047
Permit API: 015-23798
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Twp
Inspection Type: Drilling/Alteration
Inspection Date: 4/18/2023
Comments: On 4/18/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Folta well site. It was 42 degrees when I arrived on location. Chesapeake was in the process of drug testing all personnel at the site when I arrived on location. Two Chesapeake personnel were at the entrance to the site saying that everyone entering the site had to be tested. I politely refused the offer, saying that I would be tested by DEP if my employer required it. They told the drug testing personnel who were stationed outside the Chesapeake's company mans trailer that I would not be drug tested. The Chesapeake company man had the drilling safety lead, Jon Zwitzig, accompany me during the site inspection. Jon explained current operations as follows: Precision rig 573 was on site drilling the first of four new wells. The six existing wells have been shut in for the duration of the drilling and completion process. The rig was currently drilling the lateral on the Folta 22HC well. The surface and intermediate sections of all four wells were completed by a different rig that has since moved off location. Jon was unsure how long the Precision rig was expected to take to finish drilling all four wells. Jon accompanied me on the site inspection. The drilling rig and ancillary equipment is staged on plastic lined secondary containment that is protected by drilling mats. I did witness a section of drilling mats that did not have the plastic liner under them. A skid steer was on these drilling mats with a pallet of bagged chemicals that were being added to the process. I did witness white powder on the uncontained drilling mats and near the pallet of chemicals. I discussed the chemical handling and the fact that the skid steer was hauling damaged bags with Jon and that the white powder was not within secondary containment. While he did provide reasons for the crew workers working so fast, he did not provide a solution for transporting the damaged bags across the pad surface and allowing the powder to land outside of secondary containment. He did say that he would have a cew worker sweep up the current spilled substance. Drill cuttings are collected from two areas at the site; one directly east of the rig and one coming off of the centrifuges. The drill cuttings are solidified with a nutshell based compound. I screened water puddles in the southeast corner of the site with the readings being at 1.367 mS conductance or less. This is in an area that had demonstrated 10.03 mS conductance on an earlier inspection conducted by the DEP on 3/15/2023. Other water puddles at the site field tested at less than 1.0 mS conductance. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM has not been addressed at this site. A new ESCGP is pending for the location.When finishing up the inspection, the safety lead told me I needed to accompany him to get drug tested. I told him I was not going to be drug tested by Chesapeake. He told me that everybody that worked on the site had to be drug tested to be able to be there. I again told him that I was not going to be drug tested by Chesapeake and that I had unfettered access to inspect the site. I told him that my employer will drug test me if needed. I did offer to call my supervisor and let the safety person listen to the conversation while my supervisor could give a better explanation why I wasn't going to be drug tested by Chesapeake during this site inspection. He declined the invitation.The DEP recommends the following:1. Conduct good chemical handling practices to prevent causing pollution to the waters of the commonwealth. Ensure chemicals are properly contained in serviceable containers. Repair/replace damaged containers as soon as discovered.2. Inform the Chesapeake safety representatives of the DEP's right to unfettered access as described in the site permits.I left the site at 1400 hrs.

While he did provide reasons for the crew workers working so fast, he did not provide a solution for transporting the damaged bags across the pad surface and allowing the powder to land outside of secondary containment. He did say that he would have a cew worker sweep up the current spilled substance. Drill cuttings are collected from two areas at the site; one directly east of the rig and one coming off of the centrifuges. The drill cuttings are solidified with a nutshell based compound. I screened water puddles in the southeast corner of the site with the readings being at 1.367 mS conductance or less. This is in an area that had demonstrated 10.03 mS conductance on an earlier inspection conducted by the DEP on 3/15/2023. Other water puddles at the site field tested at less than 1.0 mS conductance. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM has not been addressed at this site. I told him I was not going to be drug tested by Chesapeake. He told me that everybody that worked on the site had to be drug tested to be able to be there. I again told him that I was not going to be drug tested by Chesapeake and that I had unfettered access to inspect the site. I told him that my employer will drug test me if needed. I did offer to call my supervisor and let the safety person listen to the conversation while my supervisor could give a better explanation why I wasn't going to be drug tested by Chesapeake during this site inspection. He declined the invitation.The DEP recommends the following:1. Conduct good chemical handling practices to prevent causing pollution to the waters of the commonwealth. Ensure chemicals are properly contained in serviceable containers. Repair/replace damaged containers as soon as discovered.2. Inform the Chesapeake safety representatives of the DEP's right to unfettered access as described in the site permits.I left the site at 1400 hrs.

Comments: On April 25, 2024 the Department conducted an inspection of the Augustine George 11039 access road located in Cecil Township, Washington County in regards to a complaint received on 04/24/24 CTS # 380091. The findings are as follows: At the time of the inspection, a truck was observed opening a valve and releasing what appeared to be freshwater onto the access road. Upon investigating this release, John Hulsey of Range Resources informed the Department that this fluid is freshwater and that the purpose of releasing said freshwater is to minimize the amount of dust caused from vehicles traveling up and down the access road. The released freshwater mixed with sediment as it flowed down the access road on to N Depaoli Road, traveled along the shoulder of N Depaoli and flowed off the shoulder into according to the site plans, an unnamed intermittent tributary to Millers Run. Conductivity readings were taken in the vegetation that is now impacted by sediment laden waters and they are as follows: 0.410 mS in the sediment laden puddle created from the flow going off the shoulder of the road, 0.464 mS in the vegetation adjacent to where the previous puddle reading was taken, 0.502 mS in some vegetation that is further in the intermittent tributary, and lastly 0.157 mS upslope of the Act 9 sign as a background reading. Though these readings subjugate that freshwater is being released, it is evident that sediment is still entering Waters of the Commonwealth. While onsite, the Department notified John Hulsey about the sediment entering the Waters of the Commonwealth and advised them to promptly cease all water release dust suppression activities on the access road.The Department recommends the Operator re-evaluate their dust suppression methods or implement measures to prevent sediment laden water from entering the intermittent unnamed tributary to Miller's Run.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the discharge of sediment into Waters of the Commonwealth.

Comments: On April 13, 2026, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a complaint (CTS-396434) at the Ritter well site in Redstone Township, Fayette County. The purpose of this inspection was to conduct further on-site review. An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) for this site was terminated on July 10, 2017.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of Tree Farm road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in an accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). Tree Farm Road is a township gravel road that connects to the site access road. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is on site (photo 2). Eight gas wells are onsite that appear to be equipped for production. Well 5H is equipped with a well tag with no observable evidence of a fluid leak to the ground around it (photo 17). The well and operator's information are displayed and visible on this well tag, as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h).The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection. The GPU units are not equipped with secondary containment. However, the gas wells on site were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. No evidence of a fluid leak, such as staining, was observed on the ground around the GPU units (photos 16 and 18).The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 4 and 19).The severe accelerated erosion and sedimentation remains downslope of the well pad on Tree Farm Road (photos 10-13). The Department observed a rock-lined stormwater channel along the access road, which is located upslope of Tree Farm Road. This rock-lined stormwater channel appears to be in need of maintenance, as it appears to be nearly level with the access road (photo 6). Vegetation that appears to be flattened by recent stormwater washout was observed downslope of the rock-lined stormwater channel and access road (photo 5). An erosion channel obscured by vegetation was found within the well site boundary upslope of the most severely eroded portion of Tree Farm Road (photo 14). This erosion channel appears to pose the potential to encourage channelized stormwater flow downslope to Tree Farm Road.Based on observations from this inspection, violations are being issued for failure to conduct long-term maintenance on Post-Construction Stormwater Management Best Management Practices (PCSM BMPs), which appear to be discharging excess stormwater to Tree Farm Road and resulting in accelerated erosion and sedimentation.Transmittal of this inspection report was delayed due to an IT error.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/03/2025 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/03/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8227914
Permit API: 123-47902
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/03/2025
Comments: The R H Stevenson Lease 4 conventional well is the nearest conventional well in proximity to the tank battery on the R H Stevenson lease. The tank battery is situated within earthen containment and consists of an upper level containing two stock tanks, and a lower level containing two polyurethane tanks. The stock tanks are plumbed into PVC piping that extends along the rear of the upper level of the earthen containment until terminating into the first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level. The first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level is also equipped with additional PVC piping apparently for the purpose of either removing or depositing fluids into the tank in the lower level of containment. At the time of this inspection, standing pools of fluid present in the upper level of the containment were found to have specific conductance measuring 5,980 microSiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). It was observed that straw had been laid down beneath the PVC piping in the upper level of containment. Where the straw cover ends, fluid was found to be actively flowing from the upper level of containment to the lower level. No fluid was observed to be flowing through the PVC piping connecting the stock tanks to the polyurethane tank during the time of this inspection. Neither polyurethane stock tank was found to have a noticeable volume of fluids contained within them at the time of this inspection. Some accumulation of fluids and crude oil could be observed around the base of the polyurethane tanks in the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection. The flow of fluids from the upper level to the lower level of containment was not found to be accumulating nor increasing the accumulated volume of fluids and crude oil present at the bottom of the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection.Approximately 40 feet south of the lower level tank battery containment area, crude oil and production fluids emerged on the soil surface. This flow of fluids continues west and is visually impacted by crude oil for approximately 180 feet. From there, soils and standing fluid with elevated specific conductance continue for approximately 75 feet before reaching a culvert. A pool of fluid at the entrance of the culvert was found to have specific conductance measuring 6,820 uS/cm.From the culvert, the fluid continues southwest in the natural swale for approximately 115 feet before reaching a point at which the swale transitions to an unnamed tributary (UNT) stream of Jackson Run, with defined bed and banks. At this point, waters in the UNT had specific conductance measuring 5,510 uS/cm. Specific conductance of 2,750 uS/cm was observed in the waters of the UNT in the remaining approximately 180 foot stretch, at which point there is a confluence with a second UNT of Jackson Run. Immediately before the confluence, waters in the impacted stream with specific conductance of 1,923 uS/cm were observed. Approximately two feet downstream of the confluence at a point with coordinates 41.95555, -79.29740 was the apparent end of impact to the UNTs of Jackson Run, where waters in the stream had a measured specific conductance of 42.6 uS/cm.At the time of this inspection, the well name, API number, and operator contact information was not displayed anywhere on the well.On 04/04/25 I called and spoke with William Cenk and Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. Mr. Cenk and Mr. Miller agreed to meet with Department officials onsite next week. A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 944926
Permit API: 015-23674
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Franklin Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2/11/2022
Comments: This Inspection Report cites violations for an apparent flowback (brine) release to the pad surface. The Analytical Report (attached) for SAC 942 metals shows 16.7 mg/L barium and 80.6 mg/L strontium in the liquid sample collected on February 1, 2022 (inspection 3315684). The narrative and findings in this report are from that previous inspection. I spoke with Justin Myers (Chief) on site. He explained that Cudd started drilling out plugs from the 5 Marcellus well heads today. They will have 3 coil tubing units on site to complete this job. Myers expects they will finish drilling the plugs in about 10 days. Workers are removing liner containment used while hydraulically fracturing the 5 Marcellus wells at this site. Pooled liquid on the south half of the pad surface has electrical conductivity of 14.1 - >19.99 mS/cm with an Oakton PCSTestr 35. I collected liquid sample 0935-430 in a 125 mL bottle and sent it to the DEP lab for SAC 942 metals analysis. The puddles across the south end of the pad are relatively shallow (<1/2" deep), so I did not fill a 500 mL bottle for inorganic element analysis. Violations could be cited pending laboratory sample analysis. Myers contacted Brendon Logan (Chief) to investigate the pooled liquid on the pad surface. I did not observe accelerated erosion or sedimentation during this inspection. Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Air temp 26F JLP

Comments: This inspection is being performed in response to a report of a previous spill that occurred in February. It was reported that a containment overflow allowed production water to leak and eventually run down the access road and into a vegetated area, and was not reported to DEP. It appears as though the leak source is from a valve cluster sitting along the Billy Buck Rd. Some production water leaked and was cleaned up Feb 3. However, some of the product was not collected at the time and ran down the ditch/access road approximately 150 feet before crossing the access road and running into the pipeline corridor on the south side of Billy Buck Rd. The water appears to have spread across the corridor in multiple fingers, causing a kill zone in each location. Elevated conductivity readings >20 mS were noted on the pipeline corridor. The operator was contacted regarding these findings, and further investigation will be done to determine the scope and impact of the spill.

Comments: This inspection report has been developed to document an on-site routine complete inspect, and to summarize the overall status of this well and well location. The project was recently acquired by Big Dog Energy, LLC. Applications for the transfer of all four wells permitted on the site, from Geopetro LLC to Big Dog Energy LLC, were received by the Department on August 2, 2021. An application for the transfer of the ESCGP that is currently active on the site was also received by the Department. Well number 019-21988, along with three other wells, (API ID#'s: 019-21992, 019-21993, 019-22002), were drilled and currently exist on the location. Updated well tags should be installed on each of the wells at some point in the near future. Inspection ID number's 2762573 and 2762664, (conducted in early August 2018), suggest that only well number 019-22002 was ever stimulated. Additionally, it was indicated that, at the time, RE Gas intended to plug all four wells beginning with the three that had not been stimulated. The wells were never plugged. An inspection dated 07/26/2018 (ID#:2769196) cites violations for failure to restore the well location, 78a65(a)1i and OGA3216(A). ESCGP number ESX12-019-0148 is currently active on the site. The permit was renewed by RE Gas in 2017 and is set to expire on 07/17/2022. None of the earthwork proposed in the plan was ever implemented in the field. The location consists of one very large well location and a separate tank pad. The location is overgrown and clearly has not been tended to in any way for some time. There are currently, however, no clear E&S or stabilization-related issues associated with the site.

Report Details

Violation ID: 845206
Permit API: 115-22162
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Apolacon Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2019-03-19
Comments: This administrative inspection report is created to document the Department's receipt of a Remediation Summary Report prepared by the Repsol subcontractor Resource Environmental of Montrose, PA. Kris Perritt, Environmental Specialist of Repsol submitted the report to the Department on 3/14/19. The report is in reference to a reported spill incident of (0.5) gallons of production fluid to the pad surface that was discovered on 2-14-19 at the site. The Department conducted an inspection at the site on 2-15-19. The Department and Resource recorded elevated (specific conductance) conductivity readings in the fluid spilled to the pad surface near the flowline of the 3H well. For additional details pertaining to the Department's 2-15-19 inspection report, refer to the 2-15-19 inspection report, efacts inspection ID# 2842245. The Remediation Summary Report contains the following information pertaining to the spill incident and remediation efforts. The location of the release was to snow and surficial pad material directly below a leaking union on the 3H flow line. The union was repaired, and visibly impacted snow and soil were hand shoveled into a (5) gallon bucket. The bucket was then staged in nearby secondary containment. Resource mobilized to the site as per the request of Repsol on 2/15/19 to conduct characterization and confirm remediation. Resource recorded elevated conductivity in a small depression created at the center of the excavation which measures (2) feet in width and (8) inches in length, and in soil screening locations within and around the excavation. Resource collected (2) confirmatory samples from the soil screening location within the excavation demonstrating the highest EC (electrical conductivity). The samples were sent to Test America Laboratories for analysis. Resource removed a small amount of soil from the bottom of the excavation, placed it into a container, and staged it on secondary containment. Resource used absorbents to empty the sump. Since 2/15/19, approximately (50) gallons of water have been removed from the sump, and electrical conductivity screenings have decreased below (1) millisienens/cm, ms/cm. The highest conductivity reading recorded by Resource was (6.6) ms/cm in water pooled in the excavation. Resource has concluded the spill has been visibly cleaned up, and laboratory results indicate remediation is complete. The spill volume has been revised from (0.5) gallons to (2) gallons. The Department conducted a review of the report on 3/19/19, and has concluded that no further action is warranted of Repsol at this time. Please forward the waste manifests to the Department of the material disposed of at a landfill upon receipt.

Unconventional: No
County: Washington

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection

Comments: On 06/22/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Pizzi 4 well following a Department issued Spill Order sent to the operator on 05/11/2023 via email.It is recommended to ensure that well transfer paperwork is obtained by the Department. The following was observed during inspection:Impacted substrate appeared to not have been remediated and straw applied to area (Photos 1-8); impacted material will need to be removed from site and a waste manifest provided to the Department. Elevated conductivity was observed (Photos 2-6). Fluid level in tank appeared to be lower (Photo 8).Areas of fluid that was recommended to be addressed in IR 3569077 (Photos 9, 10). Pipe observed in vegetation, which appeared to be the pipe referenced in IR 356907 associated with the fluid (Photos 11, 12).Gravel pile observed onsite (Photo 13).Regarding the access road and earth disturbance, it appears a culvert has been constructed to divert water from the excavated channel along the site access road, documented in IR 3537433 (Photos 14, 15).The culvert appears to discharge off the hillside into the woods with no riprap at the discharge point observed (Photos 16, 17). It appears that this area has potential for accelerated erosion and transport of sediment down slope (Photos 14-19).Stabilization has not been applied to disturbed area and minimal vegetation observed (Photos 14, 15, 18, 19). A permit for culvert installation has not been obtained from the Department. Violations of 102.4(b)4, 102.4(b)1, 102.22(b)1, and 102.22(a) are being issued for failure to implement the use of Best Management Practices (BMPs) including temporary stabilization, permanent stabilization, and perimeter control for the protection from accelerated erosion and sedimentation.Additional violations may be forthcoming pending further inspection.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 11/23/2022
Comments: On 11/16/22 a follow-up inspection of the McClure 3 OG Well site was conducted related to violations issued on 10/21/22 (IR:3444721). I was accompanied by Chase Ambrose (PA DEP).Background:On 10/21/22, during a routine inspection, violations were issued for a brine release at the McClure 3 OG Well Site. Elevated conductivity was observed inside the earthen containment berm that surrounds the production tank. The tank was in poor condition corroded with rust and holes. Elevated conductivity was also observed outside of the earthen berm containment.An operator response was received by the Department on 11/7/21 stating that the impacted material was removed and disposed of, the well does not produce fluid, and a new tank had been installed. Findings:-Elevated conductivity was observed in soil outside of the containment berm and in standing water inside of the earthen containment berm for the production tank (Photos #1). -The berm appeared to have recently been reworked. The substrate appeared to be uncompacted and no temporary stabilization was observed (Photos #3-4).-A new tank was present. It did not appear to have been connected to the well (Photos #5-6).-The area immediately outside of the earthen berm appeared to have been recently disturbed. No temporary stabilization was observed (Photo #6).-Some discarded pieces of pipe were observed inside the berm (Photo #7).-No outlet or shut off valve was observed for the berm drain (Photo #9).I called Bryan Goletz of Diversified to inform him of my findings. Mr. Goletz stated that he would address the spill and berm. The observed elevated conductivity indicates that the spill has not been fully remediated. Outstanding violations of 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.54 are being issued.

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 2/24/2021 to ENERVEST OPR LLC in Greene Twp, Mercer county. 78.121(A) - WELL REPORTING - PRODUCTION REPORTING - Conventional operator failed to submit annual conventional production and status report for permitted or registered well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ENERVEST OPR LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 2/24/2021
Violation Code: 78.121(A) - WELL REPORTING – PRODUCTION REPORTING – Conventional operator failed to submit annual conventional production and status report for permitted or registered well.
Violation ID: 908936
Permit API: 085-22727
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer
Municipality: Greene Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/24/2021
Comments: Field inspection performed midmorning with warm, sunny weather conditions and 55 degrees with a steady breeze. At the wellhead all valves are closed (shut-in): two closed valves on the upper and the lower production casing tubulars; valve closed on bottom tubular port; valve closed on tubular port plumbed to surface production equipment; annulus is vented via plumbed poly hose feeding tank (photo #1). Broken pressure gauge on wellhead. Some minor corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars (photo #1). The well label/marker information is missing and doesn't clearly identify well. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for well label/marker OGA3211(H). The surface/ground production equipment and one 100 bbl steel tank contained within an earthen dike was over grown with vegetation (photo #2). The tubulars feeding the ground production unit valves are closed. The steel tank exhibits moderate amounts of oxidation, but no leaks were visible (photo #2). There is no production chart present or any functional production equipment (photo #3). The well posting information is missing information and doesn't clearly identify well. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for well posting OGA3211(G). Operator has not submitted Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for 2020. Operator submitted 2019 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well stating 920 psig on the primary production casing. A broken pressure gauge was on the wellhead during inspection (photo #1). Notice of Violation (NOV) issued for mechanical integrity 78.88(a). Operator has not submitted Annual Production Report (APR) for 2020. Operator submitted annual production report (APR) for 2019 stating 0 MCF with comment that well is temporarily not producing. The Operator has reported this well like this since 2009. This well has not produced reported quantities of hydrocarbons since 2001. No house gas meter is noted on 2019 APR or present on location. Notice of Violation (NOV) issued for mechanical integrity 78.121(A) - Well Reporting Annual Production. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for well abandonment OGA3220(A).
